info.title: questlog API
info.description:
A spoiler-free quest log, build tracker and item list for the games you play. The MCP endpoint (/mcp) comes first; this API follows it, over the same data and the same rules: only the signed-in player's own log, and no spoiler unless a request asks for it.

Every error is JSON, `{"error": "...", "code": "..."}`. Besides the responses listed per operation, an unknown path answers 404 (`not_found`), a method an operation doesn't have answers 405 with `Allow`, and a failure on the server's side answers 500 (`internal`) without details.

post.description: The player's words verbatim as transcript, then what was learned from it: quests with their entries, a stat snapshot, the build plan and items. The same as the MCP tool record.

transcript.description: What the player said, verbatim, never a summary. A screenshot they shared: what it shows, written out as text and numbers

summary.description: One or two sentences of what happened in this session, in the player's terms

playthroughId.description: The playthrough, as briefing returns it. Without it, give game

game.description: The game's title, when there is no playthroughId: an unknown title starts a new game and playthrough

platform.description: For a new game: where it is played (Switch 2, PS5, PC)

label.description: Which run of the game: NG, NG+; picks or starts that playthrough

language.description: For a new playthrough: the language the game is played in (de, en)

playedOn.description: The day of the session. Default today

quests.description: Quests the player started, advanced or finished in this session

id.description: An existing quest's id, from briefing or open_threads

name.description: The quest's name, or the NPC's when the game names none. An exact match in the playthrough updates that quest; otherwise a new one starts

localName.description: The name in the game's own language, as the player said it

description.description: What it is, as the game describes it (from a screenshot or the player); replaces the one it has

notes.description: The player's own thoughts on it, in their words (never yours); added to the notes it has

tags.description: Its tags: free names to filter by across groups, like an element or a status effect. Reuse the game's tags (briefing, item and codex list them); a new one only for an idea none of them covers; one tag per idea (fire, not fire damage and fire resistance). Replaces the tags it has; leave it out to keep them

status.description: open: waiting on the player; blocked: waiting on the game; done, failed, dropped close it. Set done only when the player said they finished it. Default: unchanged, open for a new one

kind.description: log: what the player did or found out; next: the next step, in vague words; decision: a choice the player made

spoiler.description: Default none: what the player found or told. hint when the text names a place, person or item the player hasn't reached; full when it names a boss, an outcome or a story event. A next step from your own knowledge of the game is at least hint

stats.description: A snapshot of the stats, as the player said them or a screenshot shows them

values.description: Each stat by its key, as earlier snapshots name it: { "vitality": 12, "motivity": 20 }

names.description: For a stat the game hasn't had yet: its English and its own name

localName.description: The game's own name for it

notes.description: The player's own thoughts on where the build stands

build.description: The build plan, when the player set or changed it

mainStat.description: The stat key the build is built around

targets.description: Short for stat goals the player decided: { vigor: 20 }. For order or a reason, use goals

goals.description: Long-term goals the player set or changed in this session, in order; and ones you suggest, marked suggested, until they agree

id.description: An existing goal's id, from briefing, to change it (accept a suggestion, re-rank, mark reached or dropped)

kind.description: For a new goal. stat: a stat to a value; level: a character level; item: something to do with an item; note: anything else

stat.description: stat: the stat's key, as snapshots name it

target.description: stat: the value; level: the level. A new target for the same stat replaces the open goal (the old one is dropped)

item.description: item: the item's id or exact name in this playthrough

text.description: note: the goal itself. Any goal: why, in the player's terms

suggested.description: true for a goal you or a guide propose and the player hasn't agreed to yet. Default false: the player decided it

status.description: reached for an item or note goal the player finished (stat and level goals get there on their own), dropped when given up

spoiler.description: Default none. hint or full when the goal names a place, item or outcome the player hasn't reached

rank.description: Its place in the order, 1 first. Default: last; a replacing goal keeps the old one's place

notes.description: The player's own thoughts on it, in their words (never yours); added to the notes it has

character.description: Who the player plays in this playthrough, when they say or a screenshot shows it

class.description: The starting class, origin or combat memory, in English

localClass.description: The class's name in the game's own language

carryFrom.description: Starting a new playthrough (NG+) with game and label: the playthrough to take the character, build plan and open goals from. Only when the player wants it

items.description: The player's inventory: items they found, used up, equipped or put away

description.description: What it is, as the game describes it (from a screenshot or the player); replaces the one it has

notes.description: The player's own thoughts on it, in their words (never yours); added to the notes it has

kind.description: The inventory group: a key, name or local name of one of the game's groups (game.itemKinds), else a new group in the game's terms (weapon, armour, amulet, consumable, material, collectible, key, ring, talisman)

quantity.description: How many the player has now, for consumables, materials and collectibles

attributes.description: Its numbers as the game shows them, by the game's names, from a screenshot or what the player says: { "Physical ATK": 119, "Technique": "C", "Weight": 11.4 }

target.description: A codex entry (boss, enemy, NPC): its id or exact name

effect.description: How well it works on them, as the player found or a guide says. very good: its weak spot; good (the default): use it; neutral: no better or worse; bad: they resist it; very bad: they heal from it or it backfires

note.description: How or why: fire against a weak spot, throw before the second phase; it heals from fire

against.description: What the item works on, and how well

tags.description: Its tags: free names to filter by across groups, like an element or a status effect. Reuse the game's tags (briefing, item and codex list them); a new one only for an idea none of them covers; one tag per idea (fire, not fire damage and fire resistance). Replaces the tags it has; leave it out to keep them

verdict.description: How it fits the build, with where you know it from

spoiler.description: Default none. hint or full when the verdict names what the player hasn't reached

sources.description: The pages you took its facts from, with the facts; merged by link into those it has

title.description: What it is: the site's name, or the page's title

facts.description: For an item: the facts you took from the page, in your own words (scaling, weight, where found), never its text

itemKinds.description: Names the game's inventory groups when the player says what the game calls them; a group named by key gets the names, a new one goes last

key.description: What items' kind holds: amulet, ring, consumable; an existing group's key renames it

name.description: The group's name in English, as a heading: Amulets, Rings, Talismans

localName.description: The name in the game's own language: Amulette

codex.description: Bosses, enemies, NPCs and places the player met in this session, or what they learned about them: weaknesses, a strategy, a boss beaten

id.description: An existing entry's id, from codex or briefing

kind.description: For a new entry: boss, enemy (a regular foe), npc or place

name.description: Its name; an exact match of the same kind updates that entry

localName.description: Its name in the game's own language

status.description: met (default for a new one), beaten for a boss or enemy the player defeated, gone for an NPC dead or left, or a boss skipped

attempts.description: A boss: the player's tries so far, as they count them

weaknesses.description: What hurts it (fire, electric blitz, a weak spot); added to those it has

resistances.description: What it shrugs off; added to those it has

strategy.description: How to go about it, as the player found or decided; from a guide, with sources and a spoiler level

description.description: What it is: an NPC's role and wares, a place's rest point and shortcuts, a boss's lore as the game tells it; replaces the one it has

notes.description: The player's own thoughts on it, in their words (never yours); added to the notes it has

sources.description: The pages its weaknesses or strategy come from, with the facts; merged by link

tags.description: Its tags: free names to filter by across groups, like an element or a status effect. Reuse the game's tags (briefing, item and codex list them); a new one only for an idea none of them covers; one tag per idea (fire, not fire damage and fire resistance). post.description: Each change names one row by what and id and sets some of its fields, or removes it; all apply or none. The same as the MCP tool correct.

what.description: The kind of row: game, playthrough, session, quest, entry (a quest's log line), snapshot (stats), item, goal or codex (a boss, enemy, NPC or place)

id.description: Its id, as briefing, open_threads, item or record returned it

remove.description: Remove it. A game or playthrough takes everything filed in it along; a session its log entries and its snapshot; a quest its entries. Only when the player said so

mergeInto.description: A quest only: the id of the quest it really is. Its entries move there and it is removed. Only after the player agreed

status.description: playthrough: playing, finished, dropped. quest: open, blocked, done, failed, dropped; done only when the player said they finished it. goal: open, reached, dropped. codex: met, beaten, gone

playedOn.description: session (its snapshot moves with it) or snapshot: the day

localName.description: quest, item or codex: the name in the game's own language; null clears it

location.description: quest: where it started; item: where it was found; codex: where the player met it; null clears it

kind.description: entry: log, next, decision. item: weapon, armour, amulet, consumable, material, collectible, key, or the game's term; null clears it

text.description: entry; goal: the note, or why

spoiler.description: entry, item, goal or codex: none once the player has found what it names

values.description: snapshot: the stats to fix, by key; the others stay

verdict.description: item: how it fits the build, with where you know it from; null clears it

title.description: What it is: the site's name, or the page's title

target.description: goal (stat or level): the new value

quantity.description: item: how many; null when it isn't counted

attributes.description: item: its numbers, all of them: a key left out is dropped

against.description: item: what it is good or bad against, all of it: a link left out is dropped

target.description: A codex entry (boss, enemy, NPC): its id or exact name

note.description: How or why: fire against a weak spot, throw before the second phase; it heals from fire

key.description: What items' kind holds: amulet, ring, consumable; an existing group's key renames it

description.description: game, quest, item or codex: what it is; null clears it

notes.description: every target but entry: the player's own notes, all of them (this replaces them); null clears it
